problems.title: Arc length in radians
problems.question: A radius-5 circle has an arc subtending 3 radians. Find its length.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.

problems.title: Even and odd functions
problems.question: Among the six printed functions $a,b,c,d,e,f$, how many are even or odd?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: $\sin(-x)=-\sin x$, $\cos(-x)=\cos x$, $\tan(-x)=-\tan x$; domains must also be symmetric.
steps: $a(x)=2\sin x/(1+\cos x)$ is odd: its numerator changes sign and denominator does not. $e(x)=|1+\cos x|/\tan x$ is also odd, with a symmetric domain.
The numerators of $c,d$ mix an odd sine and an even cosine, so neither has parity. The denominators of $b,f$ involve $1+\sin x$, producing different values or asymmetric domains under reflection.
Thus exactly two have parity, both odd. None is even.

problems.title: Check half-angle identities
problems.question: How many of the five printed half-angle formulas are identities?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The first two printed formulas swap the plus and minus signs. The third is the reciprocal of the correct tangent-square expression.
The last two expressions give cotangent of the half-angle, not tangent. Therefore none is an identity on its allowed inputs.

problems.title: Parallel lines cut by parallel planes
problems.question: Two parallel planes are cut by two parallel lines. What quadrilateral do their four intersection points necessarily form?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: Intersections of parallel planes with a transverse plane are parallel lines.
steps: The two parallel lines lie in one plane. In this plane, the segments joining their intersections with each cutting plane are parallel.
The other opposite sides lie on the original parallel lines. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so the figure is a parallelogram.
problems.note: With an inclusive definition of trapezoid, a parallelogram is also a trapezoid. The specific guaranteed classification is parallelogram; no equal-side or right-angle condition is given.

problems.title: A quadrilateral between two parallelograms
problems.question: $ABCD$ and $ABC_1D_1$ share $AB$ in different planes. Find perimeter $CDD_1C_1$ if $AB=5.5,CC_1=4.45$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: Opposite parallelogram sides are equal and parallel.
steps: $CD$ and $C_1D_1$ are equal and parallel, each length 5.5. Also $DD_1=CC_1=4.45$ by the common translation from $D$ to $C$ and $D_1$ to $C_1$.
The perimeter is $2(5.5+4.45)=19.9$.

problems.title: Area of a circular segment
problems.question: Find the area of a radius-$\sqrt2$ circular segment with central angle $0<\alpha<\pi$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Subtract the isosceles triangle area from the sector area. Since $R^2=2$, the result is $\alpha-\sin\alpha$.

problems.title: When a sine equation is possible
problems.question: How many integers $a$ allow at least one real $x$ with $\sin x=a^2-a-1$?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: A real sine value lies in $[-1,1]$.
steps: Require $0\le a(a-1)\le2$. For integer $a$, the lower bound always holds.
The upper bound gives $(a-2)(a+1)\le0$, so $a=-1,0,1,2$.

problems.title: Shift an angle by three half-turns
problems.question: $\cos\alpha=-1/3$. Which listed angle can have sine $1/3$?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The identity gives $1/3$ immediately. For the other candidates, sine is either $\cos\alpha=-1/3$ or a signed version of $\sin\alpha$, whose magnitude is $2\sqrt2/3$.

problems.title: A common point of lines in intersecting planes
problems.question: Planes $\beta,\gamma$ meet along $a$. Lines $b\subset\beta,c\subset\gamma$ meet at $K$. Which of $K\in\beta,\gamma,a,b,c$ may be false?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: $K$ is on both $b$ and $c$, and hence in both planes. It must therefore belong to their intersection line $a$.
All five statements are necessarily true.
problems.answer: All five are true; choose the final option.

problems.title: Which distance statement can fail?
problems.question: Test: the distance between parallel objects $X,Y$ equals the distance from any object $Z$ lying in $X$ to $Y$. Which listed types can make this false?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: Distance between sets is the smallest distance between their points.
steps: The false case is $X=$ plane, $Y=$ line, $Z=$ line. Put $X:\ z=0$, $Y:\ (t,0,1)$, and $Z:\ (t,10,0)$.
The plane-to-$Y$ distance is 1, whereas the $Z$-to-$Y$ distance is $\sqrt{101}$.
For parallel planes every point on one plane has the same distance to the other; the other listed point/segment/line cases therefore do satisfy the statement.

problems.title: A false cotangent product formula
problems.question: Which of the six printed trigonometric identities is false?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Multiplication gives $(1-u^2v^2)/(u^2-v^2)$. The first printed formula has its reciprocal, so it is not an identity.
The four sum-to-product formulas and the last tangent-product formula follow from the addition formulas and are correct wherever defined.

problems.title: Integer outputs of a trigonometric expression
problems.question: How many integers can $2\sin^2x+3\cos x+4$ equal?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The expression is $-2t^2+3t+6=-2(t-3/4)^2+57/8$. Its maximum is $57/8$ and minimum is 1, attained at $t=-1$.
Continuity gives the full range $[1,57/8]$. Its integer values are 1 through 7.

problems.title: Reduce a product to one sine
problems.question: Find the least positive period of $\sin x\cos x\cos2x$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The function is $\tfrac14\sin4x$, with least period $2\pi/4=\pi/2$.

problems.title: Signed distances to a plane
problems.question: $AC:CB=2:1$ on a segment not parallel to plane $\alpha$. Distances of $A,B,C$ from the plane are $5,x,5$. Find $x$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Choose $d_A=5$. If $d_C=5$ too, the formula forces $d_B=5$, making the segment parallel to the plane, contrary to the condition.
Thus $d_C=-5$. Then $-15=5+2d_B$, so $d_B=-10$ and its ordinary distance is 10.

problems.title: Equal distances to the sides of a quadrilateral
problems.question: A point is distance $\sqrt{15}$ from every side of a quadrilateral and $\sqrt6$ from its plane. Its area is 24. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: Projected distance to each side $r=\sqrt{15-6}=3$; for a tangential polygon $S=rP/2$.
steps: Project the point perpendicularly onto the quadrilateral plane. Pythagoras gives distance 3 from the projection to every side.
With the intended internal equidistant point, join it to the vertices. The four triangle areas sum to $3P/2=24$, so $P=16$.
problems.note: This uses the intended convex tangential configuration, with the projected point inside the quadrilateral. If distances are interpreted only to extended side lines and an exterior point is allowed, that interior condition must be added.

problems.title: A trigonometric function on a short interval
problems.question: $f$ has domain $[0.35\pi,0.45\pi]$ and takes value $\sin19.9\pi$ somewhere. Which listed basic trigonometric formula can define it?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The choice $f(x)=-\cos x$ attains this value at $x=0.4\pi$, inside the domain.
The positive functions $\sin,\cos,\tan,\cot$ on this interval cannot attain a negative value. The remaining choice $-\sin x$ is below $-\sin0.35\pi$, hence too negative.

problems.title: Minimum of a sum of sixth powers
problems.question: Find the least possible value of $\sin^6\alpha+\cos^6\alpha$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: With $u=\sin^2\alpha,v=\cos^2\alpha$, the expression is $1-3uv\ge1-3/4=1/4$.
Equality holds when $\sin^2\alpha=\cos^2\alpha=1/2$.

problems.title: Combine sine and cosine
problems.question: Simplify $\sin15^\circ+\tan30^\circ\cos15^\circ$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The expression equals $(2/\sqrt3)\sin45^\circ=\sqrt2/\sqrt3$.

problems.title: Angle between lines on two dihedral faces
problems.question: $A,B$ lie on the dihedral edge. Perpendiculars $AC,BD$ lie in its different faces, with $AB=AC=BD=CD/2$. Find the angle between lines $AC,BD$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Let the common length be $t$. The edge direction is perpendicular to both $AC,BD$, so $CD^2=AB^2+|BD-AC|^2$.
Thus $4t^2=t^2+2t^2(1-\cos\theta)$, giving $\cos\theta=-1/2$. The angle between the directed perpendicular rays is $120^\circ$.
The angle between their undirected lines is the smaller supplementary angle, $60^\circ$.

problems.title: Projections of perpendicular oblique segments
problems.question: Two perpendicular segments from a point to a plane have length ratio $4:3$. Their projections have ratio $16:9$. What angle do the projections make?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Write lengths $4s,3s$ and projections $16t,9t$. Subtracting the two Pythagorean relations gives $7s^2=175t^2$, hence $s^2=25t^2$.
Then $h^2=16s^2-256t^2=144t^2$. The cosine of the projection angle is $-h^2/(16t\cdot9t)=-1$.

problems.title: Existence in a sine equation with cotangent
problems.question: How many $\alpha\in[0,2\pi)$ allow $\sin x=(\cot(\alpha/2)+\tan(\alpha/2))/(\cot(\alpha/2)-\tan(\alpha/2))$?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: The quotient simplifies to $1/\cos\alpha$, on its original domain.
steps: For a real sine value, $|1/\cos\alpha|\le1$, requiring $|\cos\alpha|=1$. In the given interval this leaves $\alpha=0,\pi$.
At 0 the cotangent is undefined; at $\pi$ the tangent is undefined. Neither is in the original domain.

problems.title: Use the triple-angle sine identity
problems.question: Simplify $1+8\sin^310^\circ$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: With $t=10^\circ$, $1/2=3\sin10^\circ-4\sin^310^\circ$.
Multiply by 2 and rearrange to get $1+8\sin^310^\circ=6\sin10^\circ$.

problems.title: Maximum zeros among tangent values
problems.question: $a_1,\ldots,a_{199}$ form an arithmetic progression. All tangent values are defined, with some zero, some positive and some negative. What is the maximum number of zeros?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: $\tan t=0$ iff $t\in\pi\mathbb Z$; $\tan t$ is undefined at $\pi/2+\pi k$.
steps: If two terms have zero tangents, their index gap times the common difference is an integer multiple of $\pi$. In lowest terms, zero indices repeat with some integer period $q$.
$q=1$ makes every tangent zero, contrary to the signs condition. $q=2$ puts the intervening terms at tangent poles. Thus $q\ge3$, allowing at most $\lceil199/3\rceil=67$ zeros.
This bound is achieved by $a_n=(n-1)\pi/3$, whose tangents repeat $0,\sqrt3,-\sqrt3$.

problems.title: A right angle and projected oblique segments
problems.question: $KH$ is perpendicular to a plane; $KA,KB$ make angles $\alpha,\beta$ with it. Given $HAB=\gamma$, $KBA=90^\circ$, find the correct relation.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Triangle $HAB$ is right at $B$, so $\sin\gamma=HB/HA$.
Thus $\sin\gamma=\cot\beta/\cot\alpha=\tan\alpha/\tan\beta$.

problems.title: Area and a line’s angle with another face
problems.question: A line in one face of an acute dihedral angle $\alpha$ makes angle $\beta$ with the edge and angle $\gamma$ with the other face. Find the area of a right triangle with hypotenuse $\sin\beta$ and acute angle $\alpha$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The line’s unit component perpendicular to the edge is $\sin\beta$; its component normal to the other face is $\sin\beta\sin\alpha$, proving the first relation.
The triangle area is $\tfrac12\sin^2\beta\sin\alpha\cos\alpha=\tfrac12\cos\alpha\sin\beta\sin\gamma$.
